q: Why did Hannah not go with her husband to the house of Yahweh for the yearly sacrifice?
a: She did not go because she was waiting until her son was weaned.

q: Why did Hannah laugh at her enemies?
a: Hannah laughed because she rejoiced in Yahweh’s salvation.

q: How would Eli bless Elkanah and his wife?
a: Eli blessed them by asking Yahweh to give them more children from Hannah.

q: What did the elders of Israel decide to do so that they could be saved from the power of their enemies?
a: The elders decided to bring the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh from Shiloh to be with them.

q: What name did Phinehas’s wife give to the baby and why did she give him that name?
a: She named the baby Ichabod, saying that the glory had departed from Israel because the Box of God had been taken.

q: What did Yahweh reveal to Samuel about Saul’s role in Israel?
a: Yahweh told Samuel that he was to anoint Saul as ruler over Israel, and Saul would save Yahweh’s people from the hand of the Philistines.

q: Why did Samuel pour a flask of oil on Saul’s head and kiss him?
a: He did this because Yahweh had anointed Saul to be a ruler over his inheritance.

q: What message did the messengers bring back to the men of Jabesh?
a: They told the men of Jabesh that they would have deliverance the next day by the time the sun was hot.

q: How was Jonathan saved from death?
a: The people redeemed Jonathan and would not allow him to die because he had brought about a great salvation for Israel.

q: How did Yahweh say that Samuel would know whom to anoint?
a: Yahweh told Samuel that he would show him what to do and that Samuel should anoint the one Yahweh told him to anoint.

q: Why did David not allow his men to attack Saul?
a: David’s heart struck him, and he said he would not stretch out his hand against his master, because he was the anointed of Yahweh.

q: What was Nabal’s wife Abigail like?
a: She had good insight and was beautiful in appearance.

q: What did Abigail do after hearing about her husband’s response?
a: Abigail hurriedly gathered provisions, put them on donkeys, and told her young men to go ahead of her, taking them to David, but she did not tell Nabal.

q: What had happened to David’s wife, Michal?
a: Saul had given her to another man as his wife.

q: Why had the Egyptian slave’s Amalekite master abandoned him?
a: His master abandoned him because he became sick three days earlier and it was difficult for him to keep traveling with the raiding band.
